widgets_values:
Style: a faded 1990s film print. Grey-green overall, only faintly warm, with a soft dusty teal-green on tile and painted surfaces that still reads clearly as teal — muted and chalky, never bright turquoise. Saturation sits low but colour is still present, roughly a quarter off normal, not drained to grey; shadows a soft grey-green rather than black; highlights an off-white with a faint green-grey cast, never cream and never gold. A single low warm sun, light ratio four to five to one, edges slightly softened — no fill, no bounce. Low to medium contrast, compressed mid-tones, a faint atmospheric softness in the air with no visible beams or shafts, gentle corner vignette, fine 35mm grain. Everything reads like a photograph found in an old family album, printed on paper that has yellowed but not browned.

The interior of a small, empty Japanese eatery, the kind of neighbourhood ramen or udon shop that has stood unchanged for decades. The room is finished in pale painted walls and a glossy green-tiled floor that catches the low afternoon sun, throwing long diagonal patches of light and shadow across the surface. In the foreground stand several worn wooden tables with matching low wooden stools, their surfaces scratched and silvered with use; a metal cup of chopsticks and a small bottle of sauce sit at the corner of the nearest table, and a soft blur of houseplant leaves occupies the lower-left corner. Along the back left wall runs a long wooden counter with a row of matching stools, behind which sits the open kitchen area: a glass display case holding rows of bowls, a stainless hood, and a hand-painted menu board above it listing dishes in Japanese with prices in red ink. To the left of the counter, an old boxy television rests atop a refrigerated drink cabinet, its screen glowing faintly, surrounded by potted plants on shelves. A round wall clock, a calendar with a small illustration, and a vertical sign reading "open" hang on the wall, while a ceiling fan and twin fluorescent tube lights mark the overhead space. At the far end, a glass door with patterned noren-style panels stands open onto a quiet street, where a low concrete wall, a house with a grey tiled roof, and leafy green trees fill the bright background; a window on the right, fitted with bamboo blinds, lets more of the warm low sun spill inward, completing the still, gently fading atmosphere of an early evening in a place no one is rushing through.
